exact_prior_proposed_values.stance: Revolutionary regimes repeatedly restricted liberty and exported it as French domination, but continued allegiance to the ideal made it central to later revolutionary belief. exact_prior_proposed_values.meaning: The prolonged replacement of the Dutch ancien régime by a unitary, representative Batavian constitution. Federalists defended inherited provincial autonomy while unitarians sought a centralized national constitution; their conflict produced deadlock before French-backed purges enabled a unitary outcome. The unitary constitution enfranchised all male citizens earning a living and abolished inherited provincial structures, guilds, oligarchic municipal government and the established Church. Radical rulers then reserved legislative seats for themselves, provoking Daendels’s June removal of the self-perpetuating government and the holding of elections.
exact_prior_proposed_values.stance: A genuinely democratic project emerged from an existing representative tradition, after deadlock and French-backed coercion. Regular elections and relatively wide internal autonomy distinguish the Batavian case; these do not amount to independent foreign policy. The supplied page344 says “Two years” after conquest while its surrounding chronology runs from 1795 to 1798; do not infer a corrected elapsed interval.

exact_prior_proposed_values.meaning: The social base, ambitions, divisions, and limited popular legitimacy of Italian supporters of the French Revolution.
exact_prior_proposed_values.stance: Urban intellectuals welcomed France as a route to reform, but French distrust of radicalism and rural hostility sharply limited their power and independence. Moderate reformers favored separate territorial reform, while radicals sought unity, sometimes through terror; by1798–1799 some Jacobins plotted against French domination. Anti-French action did not invariably reject revolutionary symbols: Langhe peasants protesting annexation in February 1799 carried miniatures of Le Peletier and Marat.

exact_prior_proposed_values.meaning: The armed popular rising of 1-2 Prairial for bread, the Constitution of 1793, and restoration of Paris popular institutions. Women urge men from workshops into action. Demands include release of patriots, an independent Commune, permanent sections and compulsory food searches as well as bread and the 1793 constitution.
